title: A longer conversation
step: Level 3, rung 7 — the door held open a while
note:
The lean is the subject. It is the only thing separating this from door-stay-03-pretend: weight on one hip, shoulder against the door edge, a hand in a pocket — a body that has been there thirty seconds and expects to stay.

The continuity:room reference to door-cover.png was removed before the first restyle round. Every rung carried both it and the continuity:ladder reference to the rung before, and their instructions contradict each other on the one thing the ladder cannot get wrong: the ladder role says match the previous rung's camera exactly, and the room role says match door-cover's camera exactly — but door-cover is a different shot, with the door open and the guest in it. Two attachments arguing about the camera is the shape of the round-1 failure. The previous rung is the room reference, and a better one: the tan-era record shows the camera holding to four pixels across four generations when each frame was attached to the last and nothing else competed. door-stay-03-onestep keeps its door-cover reference because it is the head of the ladder and has no previous rung to use instead.

The camera clause was added after round 22 of door-stay-03-handle drifted: the floor line dropped 29px, the door top rose 10px and the door widened, while the three rungs before it had held the floor line to two pixels. The ladder attachment alone did not hold it. Stating the framing as proportions of the frame put it back to the pixel on the next round.

Round 27 held every content claim and drifted the camera: the floor line fell from 680 to 699, measured the same at five separate columns, where the four rungs before it had held 677-680. It is the same failure as round 22 of door-stay-03-handle and it happened with the proportional camera clause already in place, so the clause now names the pixel row on this fixed canvas and says outright that opening the door wide does not add wall. Re-declared for cool-flat-v2 (the plaster wall) on 2026-09-04: the wall wording moved from lavender to plaster, and the floor-line instruction — 62%, 673 pixels — now defers to the attached previous rung, because the v2 ladder settled at 67% on its head and a pixel figure from the v1 ladder would have argued with the attachment. Drawn off the v2 pretend.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE: keep the framing of the attached previous rung exactly. The line where the wall meets the floor runs straight across the picture at exactly the height it has in the attached previous rung, and it must not sit lower than that. Opening the door wide and showing the porch beyond does not add wall: the amount of plaster wall above the baseboard is exactly what it is in the attached previous rung, no more. The door's top edge sits at 9.5% of the frame height and the door occupies from 75% to 93% of the frame width. Do not zoom in, do not lower the camera, and do not enlarge the door. Only one thing changes from the previous rung: the handler has settled into a longer conversation with the empty porch. She LEANS on the open door — one shoulder and forearm resting against its edge, weight dropped onto one hip so that hip is visibly higher than the other, the far leg relaxed and crossed slightly over — with her free hand pushed into her jeans pocket. Her whole posture says she has been there half a minute and is in no hurry. She faces out, talking to nobody. The porch is empty: daylight and flat spruce foliage, no visitor. Lucy holds her settled down on the bed across the room.
mustBeTrue: the wall-to-floor line sits at the same height as in the attached previous rung — 67% in this set, measured at the baseboard top — and no lower, and the handler is visibly LEANING on the open door — shoulder against its edge, weight dropped onto one hip, one hand in a pocket — rather than standing square in the doorway, the porch beyond is empty, and Lucy stays settled on her bed.
